question: Mission Indradhanush was launched by the Government of India in 2014 specifically to address which of the following immunisation goals?

answers.text: Introduce all new vaccines (rotavirus, pneumococcal, MR) into the Universal Immunisation Programme by 2020.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: New vaccine introduction is a component of the broader National Immunisation Programme expansion. Mission Indradhanush's primary objective is specifically coverage — reaching unvaccinated and under-vaccinated children, not introducing new antigens.

answers.text: Achieve and sustain full immunisation coverage of at least 90% of children and pregnant women by targeting districts with low UIP coverage.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Mission Indradhanush was designed to accelerate immunisation coverage to ≥90% by targeting the districts, blocks, and urban areas with low Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) coverage. It uses high-intensity catch-up rounds (typically 4–5 rounds per year in identified areas) for all UIP vaccines.

answers.text: Provide free nutritional supplements to all children under 5 years enrolled in anganwadis through the ICDS network.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nutritional supplementation through anganwadis is the mandate of the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, not Mission Indradhanush. Mission Indradhanush is an immunisation initiative, not a nutrition programme.

answers.text: Train one ASHA worker per village as a dedicated vaccine cold-chain manager under NHM.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cold-chain management and ASHA training are health-system-strengthening functions within NHM but are not the defining goal of Mission Indradhanush. The mission's goal is achieving ≥90% immunisation coverage in under-served populations through intensive outreach rounds.

overallFeedback.feedback: Mission Indradhanush (2014) is specifically an immunisation catch-up mission — its defining goal is achieving ≥90% full immunisation coverage in low-coverage areas by conducting concentrated outreach rounds. Do not confuse it with ICDS (nutrition) or broader vaccine introduction programmes.

Mission Indradhanush targets districts and urban areas where immunisation coverage is low, conducting high-intensity rounds to vaccinate unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children with all UIP vaccines. The goal is ≥90% full immunisation coverage at the district level.
